title: Find what you meant among drafts
intro: For each of 10 messages, you see the keywords you typed for one of your own sentence pairs, the sentence you meant, and the drafts a writing tool offers for those keywords.
Say whether any draft is what you meant (which one), whether you would send it, and how hard it was to find. The drafts are shown in the order a user would see them.

help.text: The keywords you typed (and a cue button, if you pressed one), the sentence you meant, and the drafts a writing tool offers for those keywords.

A draft says what you meant if it carries your message, even in different words or with less detail. A draft that says the opposite, asks instead of tells, changes who does it or when, or is a different message does not.
As it is: you would send it unchanged. Small edit: you would fix a word or two. No: it would need more than that, or none was right.
How hard it was to find the draft you meant (or to see that none was right).

hard.title: How hard was it to find what you meant?
hard.text: 1 = very easy, 5 = very hard. If none was right, say how hard it was to be sure of that.

pick1.title: Is this what you meant?
pick1.text: Yes if it says the message you meant (different words are fine). No if it says something else.

options.label: Yes, this is what I meant

pick3.title: Is any of these what you meant?
pick3.text: Pick the one that says the message you meant (different words are fine), or none.

send.title: Would you send it?
send.text: Think of the draft you picked. If you picked none, choose the last option.

blocks.label: Draft 3
blocks.text: Please wait for the late bus.

practice.fb: Draft 2 carries the message (the bus is late); it lacks 'again', a small edit. Draft 1 asks a question and Draft 3 asks for something else.
The draft says the opposite of what you meant, so the answer is no, and it is easy to see.
